identity.name: Kingdom of Naples (Napoleonic)
alt_names: Kingdom of Naples under Joseph Bonaparte and Murat

land.text: the mainland of the Bourbon Kingdom of Naples, taken by the French in February 1806 (Capua on 6 February, Joseph Bonaparte in Naples on 15 February)

predecessors.note: Ferdinand IV and Maria Carolina fled to Sicily, which the Bourbons kept; Gaeta held out for almost five months.

land.text: the mainland kingdom, restored to Ferdinand after 'On 23 May, the main Austrian army entered Naples'

successors.note: The page: 'Kingdoms of Naples and Sicily were finally united to create the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies' (1816). Cliopatria's Two Sicilies row starts in 1815.

capitals.name: Naples
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Naples'; Joseph Bonaparte entered the city on 15 February 1806.

rulers.name: Joachim Napoleon (Joachim Murat)
rulers.title: King of Naples
rulers.note: Deposed after the Neapolitan War; fled to Corsica and later Cannes.

correction.text: the mainland kingdom without Sicily: 'Ferdinand IV and Maria Carolina fled to Sicily, and Palermo became their new capital'; the kingdom excluded 'the Papal States and the Republic of San Marino'

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria draws 91,185 km2 for 1806-1810 and the same outline to 1814, with Sicily (76 of 89 cells) inside. Sicily stayed with the Bourbons, so the Napoleonic state is the mainland only (about 70,000 km2; Murat's 'attempt to annex Sicily' failed). The infobox gives no area to compare. Cliopatria starts the shape in 1806, the proclamation year (30 March 1806).
91,327 km2 for 1811-1813: same correction as 1806, Sicily removed. The page records no territorial change in these years (Capri was taken from the British in October 1808, a sub-cell island).
91,185 km2 for 1814, Sicily removed. The page does not say what changed in 1814 (Murat's change of side is not on it).

correction.text: the mainland kingdom until the Austrians entered Naples on 23 May 1815

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's row ends in 1814 but the kingdom lasted into May 1815 (Tolentino 2-3 May, Treaty of Casalanza 20 May, Austrians in Naples 23 May). The Neapolitan advance into the Papal States and northern Italy is an occupation in the ledger, not territory. From the restoration Cliopatria draws the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies (kingdom-of-the-two-sicilies).

ledger.note: 30 March 1806: Napoleon makes his brother Joseph King of Naples. 'On 30 March 1806, Napoleon signed an act at the Tuileries' (infobox 'Proclamation: 30 March 1806'); Capua fell to the French on 6 February and 'On 15 February, Joseph Bonaparte solemnly entered the city of Naples'. A client state of the French Empire until 1808. The mainland only: the Bourbons kept Sicily.

region.text: the Kingdom of Naples without Sicily

ledger.note: 1806: Gaeta resists the French. The fortress 'fell after a siege of almost five months', which let the British 'have a harbor to shelter their ships'; the page gives neither start nor end month. Calabria is a second front: 'British troops defended Calabria and even scored a victory at Maida on 4 July'. Gaeta is not in the gazetteer (15 km disc).

18 July 1806: Gaeta capitulates. Siege of Gaeta (1806) infobox '26 February - 18 July 1806'; the white flag went up 'On the morning of 18 July'. Reviewer fix 2026-10-25 (eu-13-j review): was confidence 1 with the month read from 'almost five months' on the Kingdom of Naples (Napoleonic) page.

October 1808: Capri taken from the British. 'In October 1808, General Jean Maximilien Lamarque captured the island of Capri from the British.' A sub-cell island: the disc resolves to no gazetteer land cell.

15 March 1815: Murat declares war on Austria. 'declared war on Austria on 15 March 1815', five days before Napoleon's return to Paris; he arrived in Rimini on 30 March and issued his proclamation. The page does not date the first ground taken; the zone is the Marche, the Po plain and Emilia.

region.text: the Marche and the Po plain from Bologna to Ferrara

ledger.note: April 1815: Murat's army holds Bologna and the Marche. 'established his headquarters at Ancona and advanced on the road towards Bologna'; Bologna was taken on 3 April. The Papal States are the owner; the page gives no date for the Marche.
April 1815: Neapolitan troops occupy Modena. 'Carrascosa's division immediately occupied Modena' after the Battle of the Panaro, which the page does not date; April is my reading from Bologna's date.
By 8 April 1815: Neapolitan troops are in Florence. The page has Murat's troops at their zenith, holding Bologna, Modena and Florence by about 8 April while besieging Ferrara.
2-3 May 1815: Tolentino. 'give battle at Tolentino on 2 May 1815'; after two days Murat retreated. 'On 20 May, Neapolitan Generals Pepe and Carrascosa sued for peace' (Treaty of Casalanza).

region.text: the Marche and the Po plain from Bologna to Ferrara

ledger.note: May 1815: the Neapolitan troops leave the Marche and Bologna after Tolentino; the page gives no withdrawal date.
May 1815: Modena is left. Bridging entry; the page gives no date.
May 1815: Florence is left. Bridging entry; the page gives no date.

23 May 1815: the Austrians enter Naples and the Napoleonic kingdom ends. 'On 23 May, the main Austrian army entered Naples,' restoring Ferdinand; the Treaty of Casalanza was concluded on 20 May. Murat 'was forced to flee to Corsica and later Cannes.' The Neapolitan War page: the kingdoms of Naples and Sicily were united as the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies in 1816.

region.text: the mainland kingdom, returned to Ferdinand

wars.name: French conquest of the Kingdom of Naples (1806)
wars.outcome: The French took Capua on 6 February and Naples on 15 February 1806; Napoleon proclaimed Joseph King on 30 March; Gaeta fell after almost five months; the British won at Maida on 4 July; the Bourbons kept Sicily.
wars.note: The page does not name the war; the Wikipedia article for it is not opened. The French side is the Empire, not yet the Napoleonic kingdom.

wars.name: Neapolitan War

zones.text: the Marche and the Po plain from Bologna to Ferrara

wars.outcome: Murat declared war on 15 March 1815, took Bologna on 3 April, failed to cross the Po on 8 April, was beaten at Tolentino on 2-3 May and sued for peace at Casalanza on 20 May; the Austrians entered Naples on 23 May and Ferdinand was restored.
wars.note: The Austrians 'consolidated their gains in Northern Italy into the Kingdom of Lombardy-Venetia'.

certainty.note: No treaty line is on the pages opened for the Papal frontier; Calabria was held against a British-backed resistance in 1806; the sea frontier with Sicily is sharp.

notes:
Cliopatria's 'Kingdom of Naples (Napoleonic)' row (1762-1814, seven shapes) is two states: the Bourbon Kingdom of Naples and Sicily (shapes 1762, 1799, 1800, 1803, see kingdom-of-naples-bourbon, written in this batch) and the Napoleonic Kingdom of Naples of this dossier (1806-1815, shapes 1806, 1811, 1814). Both dossiers list the Cliopatria Name; this one reviews only its own years, so the validator lists the four Bourbon-era shapes as unreviewed here.
Cliopatria errors: all three Napoleonic shapes contain Sicily, which the Bourbons kept (the new 1815 keyframe and the Bourbon dossier's new 1806 keyframe carry it); the row ends in 1814 although the kingdom lasted to 23 May 1815.
Not opened (page budget): the Treaty of Casalanza and Congress of Vienna pages, the Wikipedia pages for the Calabrian resistance, Benevento and Pontecorvo (given to Talleyrand and Bernadotte in 1806, page silent) and the 1810 Papal annexations (page silent), Joseph's reforms. Gaeta and Capri are not in the gazetteer and resolve to nothing (Capri) or discs (Gaeta). Murat's 1810 attempt on Sicily is on the page without a date and is not in the ledger. Counterparts used that need a dossier from others: none new (kingdom-of-the-two-sicilies, papal-states, duchy-of-modena-and-reggio, grand-duchy-of-tuscany, austrian-empire exist or are in eu-20). The reading 'by 8 April Florence was occupied' is the page's summary as read; a gap-filler should confirm it against the Neapolitan War page.
